57.0.0.en: "The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil. He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness." [1-2].

57.1.0.en: Here the prophet speaks of what befalls the children of God throughout the generations, as they fall under many afflictions without cause, wounded like their Savior even in the houses of their loved ones (Zech 13:6), finding enmity even from their own household (Mt 10:36). But the prophet speaks here rather of the age of King Manasseh, who shed much innocent blood (2 Kgs 21; 2 Chr 33), so that the righteous desired death and counted it a rest from what they saw with their own eyes. This applies even more clearly in the days of the Antichrist, when the man of sin reigns in the temple of the Lord and persecutes the Church (2 Thess 2:4 etc.), until it is said: "Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?" (Rev 13:4), "And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations... Here is the patience and the faith of the saints" (Rev 13:7, 10). Before this bitterness it is said: "the righteous is taken away from the evil" [2].

57.1.1.en: When the righteous are destroyed, or persecuted and killed, no one gives thought to it, for the wicked live in amusement like little children without understanding, while their parents and the loving ones who serve them die and they do not know it. But the righteous rejoice in death, counting it a release of their souls from the atmosphere that kills the soul, the atmosphere of hateful evil.

57.1.2.en: * "In his letter to a young widow."

57.1.3.en: Truly, if he had perished altogether, or if his affair had come to a complete end, that would have been a great calamity, and the matter would have been grievous. But if all that has happened is that he has sailed to a calm harbor and made a journey to God, who is in truth his King, then we must not grieve but rejoice. For this death is not death; it is rather a kind of emigration and a passing from the worse to the better, from earth to heaven, from among men to the angels and archangels, and indeed to be with God, the Lord of the angels and archangels... Now he is in great safety and calm.

57.1.4.en: * If your husband had walked like those who live a shameful life that does not please God, it would have been better for you to lament and weep, not only at his departure, but even while he was alive here. But inasmuch as he is one of the friends of God, we must rejoice in him, not only while he is alive here but also when he falls asleep in rest... Listen to what the Apostle says: "Having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better" (Phil 1:23).

57.1.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * What a benefit we gain by departing from this world!

57.1.6.en: When the disciples grieved because Christ, the Teacher of our salvation and the Teacher of our good works, announced to them that He would depart, He said to them: "If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father" (Jn 14:28); teaching us to rejoice, and not to grieve, when one of our loved ones departs from this world, truly remembering the saying of the blessed Apostle Paul: "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (Phil 1:21); counting death the greatest gain... For by death we leave behind painful toils and are delivered from the poisonous fangs of Satan, to go to the calling of Christ for us, rejoicing in eternal salvation.

57.1.7.en: The martyr Cyprian * He fears death who awaits another death after death.

57.1.8.en: * By death the children escape the afflictions that exceed their strength, obtaining the happiness that is the reward of their patience and innocence.

57.1.9.en: The martyr Cyprian St. Augustine sees that what is stated here about the death of the righteous, with no one taking it to heart, points to the Lord Christ, whom the wicked wanted to destroy by crucifixion, and they did not realize that He had permitted this in order to save what had been lost and destroyed. As the Apostle Paul says: "for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" (1 Cor 2:8).

57.2.0.en: 3 "But draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore. 4 Against whom do ye sport yourselves? against whom make ye a wide mouth, and draw out the tongue? are ye not children of transgression, a seed of falsehood, 5 Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks? 6 Among the smooth stones of the stream is thy portion; they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou poured a drink offering, thou hast offered a meat offering. Should I receive comfort in these? 7 Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed: even thither wentest thou up to offer sacrifice. 8 Behind the doors also and the posts hast thou set up thy remembrance: for thou hast discovered thyself to another than me, and art gone up; thou hast enlarged thy bed, and made thee a covenant with them; thou lovedst their bed where thou sawest it. 9 And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst increase thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers far off, and didst debase thyself even unto hell. 10 Thou art wearied in the greatness of thy way; yet saidst thou not, There is no hope: thou hast found the life of thine hand; therefore thou wast not grieved. 11 And of whom hast thou been afraid or feared, that thou hast lied, and hast not remembered me, nor laid it to thy heart? have not I held my peace even of old, and thou fearest me not? 12 I will declare thy righteousness, and thy works; for they shall not profit thee. 13 When thou criest, let thy companies deliver thee; but the wind shall carry them all away; vanity shall take them: but he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land, and shall inherit my holy mountain."

57.2.1.en: The righteous suffer from the wicked, but what can the wicked do to them? For even death the righteous count a divine gift, through which they pass from the gloomy atmosphere to enjoy the joyful meeting with the Bridegroom of their souls. But the wicked the Lord summons to judgment, in which the following takes place:

57.2.2.en: a. The wicked bear several titles, among them:

57.3.0.en: * Sons of the sorceress: the whole nation rejected the true words of the prophets and resorted to sorcery and divination to know the future and to seek counsel. This is counted a rejection of belonging to God and an acceptance of sonship to the devil and his evil works, so the wicked were counted sons of the sorceress who mocks God [4].

57.3.1.en: * The seed of the adulterer and the whore [3]: they have no relation to the righteous life, neither on the father's side nor on the mother's; the father is an adulterer and the mother a whore. Thus corruption has come upon all, men and women.

57.3.2.en: They boasted that God was their Father and Zion their mother, but their abominations revealed their true condition: they forsook belonging to God and His Church in order to belong to the evil one and his kingdom. The Evangelist says: "They said to him, We be not born of fornication; we have one Father, even God. Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I proceeded forth and came from God... Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning... for he is a liar, and the father of it" (Jn 8:41-44).

57.3.3.en: * Children of transgression [4], because they refused to obey God and to respond to His prophetic declarations and commandments.

57.4.0.en: * A seed of falsehood [5]; they deal with their faults by lying and deceit, instead of frankness and clarity.

57.4.1.en: b. Their immersion in idol worship with intense impulsiveness, setting up idols, enflaming themselves under every green tree, and offering their children as human sacrifices, burning them for the sake of Baal and Ashtaroth [5]. This hideous picture, in which men declared their ingratitude toward God and toward their children, still exists in one form or another today. Instead of thanking Him for His gifts (the green tree), we sometimes offer our hearts, inflamed with evil, for the sake of the devil and his kingdom, as unclean standards set up in the hearts; and instead of caring for our inner life so that we may enjoy spiritual fruits for soul and body, that is, begetting sons and daughters in our hearts who praise God, we offer the powers of soul and body as human sacrifices for the sake of the enemy of good.

57.5.0.en: c. Their practice of evil in the valleys [6] as on the high mountains [7] and in the houses [8]... as though evil were not tied to place or circumstances, but to the heart that has turned away from its Creator and wanted independence from Him.

57.5.1.en: Perhaps he also wanted to stress that the wicked, in their shamelessness, do evil openly and in secret, in public places as well as inside houses.

57.6.0.en: d. The wicked are likened to an adulterous woman who is not satisfied with evil but enlarges her bed [8] to accept entering into a covenant with anyone and uniting with any man, instead of uniting with God as the sole Bridegroom of her soul and making an everlasting covenant with Him. She loved the wicked not for their persons, but for the sake of lying with them as an opportunity to satisfy the lusts of the body [8].

57.6.1.en: e. She set up remembrances -drawings or statues- for those with whom she commits evil; instead of repenting she boasts of evil. Perhaps by remembrances he meant the setting up of pagan statues as spiritual adultery, and attachment to strange gods instead of God her husband, or because adultery was joined to idolatry in her life.

57.7.0.en: f. She adorned herself and anointed herself with perfumes and sent messengers to the king to commit evil with her, and so descends to hell [9]. Perhaps by the king here he meant Pharaoh, to whom they sent that he might rescue them from Assyria, and God counted this deed spiritual adultery, being reliance on the arm of man instead of trust in God.

57.7.1.en: Her sending to the king points to her union with authority, as will happen in the days of the Antichrist, when perverted religious work will be joined to worldly power, so that opposition to the Church will come through blasphemy together with the use of violence against her.

57.8.0.en: g. She seeks evil diligently in many journeys until weariness overtakes her without her despairing; because of the desire for evil she neither weakens nor tires [10].

57.9.0.en: h. She commits evil without fear of God; she did not respond either to His threats, since she did not bear the fear of the Lord [11], nor to His encouragement of her by pointing out her good works [12].

57.9.1.en: i. Her reliance on her lovers and those who desire her, as crowds who admire her; yet all of them are carried away together with her as by the wind, or are blown away with a breath, and are not found.

57.9.2.en: Perhaps by her lovers he meant the pagan gods, since she cried to them without finding any response from them, for they are unable to offer salvation; the Lord scatters her together with them like wind and like a swift breath.

57.10.s.en: 3. The blessings of returning to God:

57.10.0.en: 14 "And shall say, Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way, take up the stumblingblock out of the way of my people. 15 For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones. 16 For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth: for the spirit should fail before me, and the souls which I have made. 17 For the iniquity of his covetousness was I wroth, and smote him: I hid me, and was wroth, and he went on frowardly in the way of his heart. 18 I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners. 19 I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him. 20 But the wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt. 21 There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked."

57.10.1.en: Despite the corruption and spiritual adultery they have committed, God awaits their return to Him in repentance, to grant them the following blessings:

57.10.2.en: a. They inherit the land as a way by which they pass to the eternal inheritance. As the Lord says: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth" (Mt 5:5), and it is written in the Psalm: "For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the LORD, they shall inherit the earth" (Ps 37:9). "But he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land, and shall inherit my holy mountain. And shall say, Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way" [13-14].

57.10.3.en: If the land here points to Canaan and the holy mountain of the Lord points to Zion, then repentance grants man enjoyment of the divine blessings in this world as a pledge of the heavenly Jerusalem.

57.10.4.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that God has promised us a heavenly dowry: "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man" (1 Cor 2:9) [He appointed these as a dowry, namely: immortality, the praise of the angels, deliverance from death, freedom from sin, the inheritance of the Kingdom, whose wealth is so great, righteousness, sanctification, deliverance from present evils, the discovery of the blessings to come. Great is my dowry...! The betrothal gifts are the present blessings that make us long for the blessings to come, but the dowry in its fullness is given in the other life].

57.10.5.en: If the "land" points to the body, then the pledge we receive here is to possess the body, that is, to hold authority over it, so that we may live holy in the body by the Spirit of God who dwells in us.

57.10.6.en: By saying "Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way" [14], He means our receiving Christ our Savior as "the Way", by whom and in whom we enjoy the eternal inheritance.

57.10.7.en: b. The removal of the stumblingblock, as it is said: "take up the stumblingblock out of the way of my people" [14].

57.11.0.en: c. God's dwelling in their midst, as they are counted the high and holy mountain of God [15]. To the degree that they humble themselves in their own eyes, God exalts them and counts them worthy of His dwelling, as it is said: "I dwell... with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones" [15].

57.11.1.en: * He is far from the proud, near to the humble; "Though the LORD be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly" (Ps 138:6). The proud do not think of themselves that they are unseen, "but the proud he knoweth afar off" (Ps 138:6). He saw the Pharisee from afar, since he boasted of himself, but the tax collector was near to Him that He might help him, because he confessed (his sins) (Lk 18:9-14).

57.11.2.en: St. Augustine * Pride, even if righteousness, fasting and the paying of tithes accompany it, sees its chariot driven backward; but humility of spirit, even if sin accompanies it, outstrips the horse of the Pharisee, even if the one who leads it is poor!

57.11.3.en: St. John Chrysostom d. Even if God, as a chastener, is angry with the wicked, yet He is the Creator of souls who desires their salvation and their return to Him; therefore He does not contend for ever, nor is He always wroth, but wants everyone to return to Him, that He may heal every weakness and lead the people Himself and restore to them His comforts, as He says:

57.12.0.en: "For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth" [16]. As St. Augustine says, the troubles we endure here are because of God's wrath (against our sins) so that we may repent.

57.12.1.en: He continues the discourse thus: "for the spirit should fail before me, and the souls which I have made" [16]... God, who created human souls, will not abandon them, but longs for their salvation and works for it.

57.13.0.en: "For the iniquity of his covetousness was I wroth, and smote him: I hid me, and was wroth, and he went on frowardly in the way of his heart. I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners" [17-18].

57.13.1.en: The blows that befall him are divine wrath, for God in His love hides and is wroth in order to strike His children for a time. Perhaps by hiding here he meant that He cannot bear to see His children under pain and distress, so He is like one who strikes and hides for a moment, in order to draw His children to Himself through hardship. Therefore He affirms that even if He seems to have hidden, His eyes are on the ways of those being chastened by Him, so that He may heal them and lead them Himself and compensate their mourning with divine comforts. What a surpassing, fatherly divine love!

57.13.2.en: * If you suffer evil and bear it with gentleness, all evils will be removed from you.

57.13.3.en: * Such is the compassionate love of God. He will not turn His face away from sincere repentance, for even if a man has rushed into evil to the very end, when he chooses to return to the virtuous life God receives him and welcomes him and does all that is for his restoration, and brings him back to his first state.

57.14.0.en: St. John Chrysostom e. He pours out upon them double peace while the wicked are filled with turmoil, as He says: "I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him. But the wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt. There is no peace (joy), saith my God, to the wicked" [19-21].

57.14.1.en: He calls those who are far off (unbelievers) and those who are near (fallen believers) to come to Him in repentance and receive double peace. As St. Augustine says: [The Lord promised true consolation in the words of Isaiah: "I will give him true comfort, peace upon peace" [17] (LXX). Without this consolation men find themselves amid earthly gladness that is dissolution more than rest]. And also: [What the wicked man calls joy is not joy].
